canonical.title: Course Schedule II — Return a Valid Course Order
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/3. Topo Sort Problems/04. Course Scheduler 2.cpp

narrative.title: Publishing the Training-Pass Timetable
narrative.scenario: With the feasibility question settled, the registrar now needs an actual timetable: a listing of every training pass in an order that never violates a single requirement. Many legal timetables may exist — any one is acceptable — but circular requirements still force the registrar to publish nothing at all.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer numCourses and a list prerequisites where each pair [a, b] means course b must be taken before course a.
narrative.outputFormat: Return one valid ordering of all courses, or an empty array if no valid order exists.

testCases.explanation: Course 0 unlocks both 1 and 2; this queue order happens to admit 2 before 1.
The circular requirement means no timetable can ever be published.

hintLevels: Level 1: Same peeling trick as the feasibility check — but now record the peeling order itself.
Level 2: Append each indegree-zero course to the timetable as it is dequeued.
Level 3: A timetable shorter than numCourses is the cycle signal — return the empty list.
